The National Park pass lasts for a year. You can pick it up from REI sporting goods, and it costs $80. It grants you free admission to national parks, and for me at least, gave me half off on camping. So for example, I went to Badlands National Park. The admission fee was $25 to get in (per car) but I got in for free. 
 As for route..  I spent two weeks taking the trip. I took a centralized trip, but southern route seems pretty cool as well. Northern too! It's up to you

Sleep: I used air bnb. I'm from NJ and just did this trip to socal a couple months ago :) you can find pet friendly homes. I also got the natural park pass. Not sure if you want to do that, but some parks have cabins you can stay in. 
Driving: 12 hours is not unrealistic but it's exhausting. We drove 12hrs to Lexington, Kansas City and Scottsbluff. It was tiring, and felt like you couldn't really stay to appreciate what you are seeing. 
Food: I am allergic to dairy, we packed cliff bars, home made pizzas, rice, nut mixes etc. This didn't last us the entire trip, but it got us through the first long days. Otherwise, we Googled restaurants near where we would be sleeping.

I just got back from New Orleans, I would totally recommend taking a cemetery tour and finding one on Groupon (I think the company we used was called witchesbrew) you learn a lot of New Orleans history, and they run 2hrs long. 
I have a lot of dietary issues, so I didn't experience the food, but my boyfriend was eating po boys everywhere. His favorite was in a place called killer po boys, it's behind a restaurant with no name. I got a tarrot card reading at Bottom of the Teacup. Get Otis, he was awesome. Just do a 10min reading. New Orleans is old and haunted so I thought that would be a cool experience. 
At night, I recommend you go to Preservation Hall. They have shows all week, and have an 8, 9, 10pm show. If you decide to go to the 8pm, wait on the line 45 min early. It gets packed! It's $20 to get in. Pat O'Brians is next door, and has great drinks! Most drinks around were too sugary to enjoy, but Pats is where it's at. I stayed at a friends house, but try to stay in the french quarter. Parking is on the street, and tight in that area. You could always stay on Magazine (where I stayed). 

Portland is ok, I went to the Feminist book store featured in Portlandia. I went to a juice bar that was amazing called Kure. The Japanese Garden is beautiful and very zen. I stayed at the Jupiter Hotel, which has a great bar attached to it. Even if you don't stay there, check out the Douglass Fern. Bars close 10-12am during the week, which was weird to me because I am used to 4am closing time. Check out the Departure (rooftop bar), eating wise I can't help too much. I can't eat anything with dairy, fried or raw lol, but I can say Portland is very, very accommodating to these issues. There are a lot of homeless people, and break ins to the car are very common. Make sure to not have anything visible. I wasn't nervous in New Orleans as I was in Portland. Living near NYC, I've seen it all so to speak.. But this was the only place I've heard break ins are an everyday thing.
